hints: Look closely at lactic acid, it has two different kinds of -OH, one in an alcohol and one in a carboxylic acid.
Remember that the carboxylic acid -OH is strongly acidic, while the alcohol -OH is only very weakly acidic, so few reagents attack both.
Think about which reagent is reactive enough to release hydrogen gas from both an acid and an alcohol to form salts.
walkthrough:
**Spot the two different -OH groups**

Lactic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$, is bifunctional. It has a secondary alcohol group, $\text{-CH(OH)-}$, and a carboxylic acid group, $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$.

They behave differently because the $\text{O-H}$ in $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ is much more acidic.

**Recall what attacks each group**

Oxidising agents oxidise the secondary alcohol but leave the carboxylic acid alone. Bases like $\text{NaOH}$ neutralise the carboxylic acid but are not strong enough to react with a neutral alcohol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H} + [O] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCO}_2\text{H} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Find the reagent that does both**

Sodium metal is a very strong reducing agent that reacts with any labile $\text{O-H}$ proton to give hydrogen gas. It forms both an alkoxide from the alcohol and a carboxylate from the acid.

$$2\text{R-OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{R-ONa} + \text{H}_2$$
$$2\text{RCO}_2\text{H} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RCO}_2\text{Na} + \text{H}_2$$
So sodium reacts with both -OH groups.

options.A: Acidified potassium dichromate(VI) is an oxidising agent. It oxidises the secondary alcohol group to a ketone (pyruvic acid), but it does not react with the carboxylic acid group which is already fully oxidised.
options.B: Ethanol can undergo esterification with the carboxylic acid group to form an ester plus water. It does not react with the alcohol -OH group under normal conditions, so only one group reacts.
options.C: Sodium reacts with both acidic protons. It reacts with the carboxylic acid to give sodium lactate plus hydrogen, and with the alcohol group to give an alkoxide plus hydrogen. It is reactive enough to attack even the weakly acidic alcohol -OH.
options.D: Sodium hydroxide is a base that neutralises the carboxylic acid in an acid-base reaction to give sodium lactate plus water. Alcohols are too weakly acidic to react with NaOH, so the alcohol -OH is left unchanged.
